x: Gordon Doubleday, who completed the course in 47 minutes less time than last year, won a handicap prize presented by Charlie Poulter. The race was well supported by Club members and friends and with the weather in our favour, a good time was had by all.

Perhaps the most surprising performance of all was that of George Oliver, who, competing in his first Brighton, finished 18th, just outside first class standard and very deservedly won a special handicap prize presented by Charlie Poulter.

Particular mention must be made of Charlie Poulter and his two lads who carried a vast quantity of tea from London to Arrowe Park, where he was soon relieved of it by three teams of thirsty and grateful runners.

Front: B. Trower. D. Baulch
Back: P.Bagnall. J.Masters.,E.Gebbett.E.Patterson.C.Poulter Masseur.
Our thanks are due to all our helpers and supporters, notably Arthur Whitehead and his Dor-mobile NAAFI waggon and Charlie Poulter and his equipment, so welcome at the end of a gruelling race.
